html:
Logistic sigmoid σ(z) = 1/(1+e−z)

Drag the black point along the curve to read exact (z, σ(z)) coordinates. Slide τ to find the z-value where the sigmoid crosses a decision threshold — that's the log-odds ln(τ/(1−τ)).

authoredPrompt: This figure shows the logistic sigmoid function sig[z] plotted as a single smooth curve over the range z ∈ [−5, 5]. The horizontal axis is labeled z with tick marks at −5.0, 0.0, and 5.0, and the vertical axis is labeled sig[z] with tick marks at 0.0 and 1.0. A smooth orange S-shaped curve rises monotonically from near zero on the left to near one on the right, with its steepest slope occurring at z = 0 where the function equals exactly 0.5. Gray dashed lines indicate the horizontal asymptote at sig[z] = 1.0 and mark a vertical reference at z = 0, emphasizing the function’s symmetry and its asymptotic approach to both bounds. This figure introduces the logistic sigmoid as a differentiable, bounded activation function that squashes any real-valued input into the interval (0, 1), motivating its use for modeling probabilities in binary classification.
authoredInteractions:
- Drag a point along the sigmoid curve to display the exact coordinate pair (z, sig[z]) at that position
- Slider for a probability threshold: draw a horizontal line at the chosen value and mark the corresponding z intercept where the sigmoid crosses it

discrepancies: the y-axis title is garbled: it renders as 'sig[' floating above the frame (the 'z]' portion is detached/missing) instead of 'sig[z]' centered vertically beside the axis, caused by the conflicting rotate-transform plus .center() call
an orphaned '1' text element (ftext, never positioned) renders as a stray glyph at the top-left corner of the figure
the σ=0.5 reference line spans the full plot width as a blue dashed line, whereas the source shows a short gray dotted segment from the y-axis to the curve at z=0

two redundant readout labels ('σ(z) = 0.50 → z = ln(τ/1−τ) = 0.00' and 'z = 0.00, σ(z) = 0.500') crowd the curve midpoint in the default state, and the threshold label starts left of the frame edge, overlapping the y-axis tick-label area
a black dot marker sits at (0, 0.5) in the default view, which does not appear in the source
the minor tick marks along the left/top/right frame edges present in the source are missing
evaluation.notes: The sigmoid curve, boxed frame, ticks, and fraction annotation faithfully reproduce the source and the threshold-slider plus draggable-point interactions are rich and correct, but the default view is marred by a garbled y-axis title, a stray '1' glyph, and cluttered/escaping readout labels.
action_items: Remove the orphaned ftext element (draw.text with tspan '1' that is never positioned) so no stray '1' renders at the top-left corner.
Rebuild the y-axis title as a single rotated text 'sig[z]' centered beside the axis; drop the conflicting .transform({rotate...}) + .center() combination that scatters the tspans.

Keep the threshold label inside the plot frame (clamp its x so it never starts left of the box) and suppress or merge the point readout when it duplicates the threshold readout at default, so the two labels stop crowding the curve midpoint.
Style the default σ=0.5 reference to match the source: a short gray dotted segment from the y-axis to the curve, and add the minor ticks along the frame edges.
